title: Control Plane
what: The logic that decides how traffic should be handled.
why: A network needs centralized decision-making for policy and routing intelligence.
when: When the network requires centrally managed rules and traffic engineering.
example: The SDN controller decides traffic paths for network segments.
scenarioApplication: Campus or enterprise networks with many switches and policy changes.

title: Data Plane
what: The forwarding path that moves packets according to installed rules.
why: Traffic must be carried quickly and consistently based on network policy.
when: Whenever traffic moves from source to destination.
example: A switch forwards frames based on the table installed by the controller.
scenarioApplication: Every network design stage, but especially dynamic traffic control.

title: Flow Management
what: The control of how traffic flows across the infrastructure.
why: To enforce quality, security, and efficient routing based on policy.
when: When multiple service paths or priority classes must coexist.
example: Institute access policies with route prioritization and inspection.
scenarioApplication: Multi-tenant or enterprise networks with distinct service classes.
